03 · The signal

The glitch that wasn't a glitch.

Two kinds of queries kept spiking, in the same places, every year: shoppers typing a size, and shoppers typing “near me” or “pick up Saturday.” Search treated both as noise, because neither fit how results were organized. The read was different: if this keeps happening, there's a reason.

Size
41%

of apparel and footwear returns said “doesn't fit,” the #1 return reason. Size went in as free text and came out as free text. The seller knew which 12 they meant. The platform didn't.

AI Size Intelligence case study
Local intent
11%

of 500 traced searches with local words ended in a local pickup. 41% left for another app mid-search, 27% left at the shipping price, and 21% got stuck in filters.

Agentic Local Pickup case study
04 · The worked examplesSize

Size 8 has eight meanings.

A shopper types one number. Before search can filter, it has to know the category, gender, fit and country behind it. Size isn't a value. It's a token that has to be disambiguated.

8
one input
US Women's clothingUS Men's shoe UK apparelEU 38 mapped JP 24.5cm shoeBrand A ≠ Brand B Narrow / Wide fitKids vs adult

“nike air max 90 size 10”: Men’s 10 and women’s 10 tiles applied, then one question

ebay.com/sch/i.html
Final comp · Desktop · Size Filter System
Final comp · Mobile · Size Filter System

Free text keeps the number and drops the context that gives it meaning. The techniques we landed on are calibrated to how sure the system is:

Sure · 90% and up

Act quietly

Apply the size and pin a receipt with one-tap Undo. Size 11 on Jordans just applies men's 11. EU 42 converts and includes US M8.5, US W10 and UK 7.5 listings.

Unsure · 50 to 89%

Ask once

Friendly chips with the translations printed on them, results still visible behind the question. Size 10 on Air Max 90 asks: Men's 10 or Women's 10?

Weak signal · under 50%

Educate, don't filter

Show the full results with size guidance inline. Never guess a filter the shopper didn't give, so nothing they wanted gets hidden.

Dropped along the way: the blocking modal (it punished experts), silent personalization (it tested as creepy), and “fix the data first” (a multi-year wait).

Local intent

eBay couldn't hear “near me.”

Buyers typed “couch near me, pick up Saturday.” Search heard “couch,” sent a sectional from 800 miles away with $120 of freight, and they left for Facebook Marketplace. We tried three ways to respond.

A · Dropped

Always push local

Felt pushy. People learn to ignore the module, and then they ignore us.

B · Dropped

Always ask first

You typed “pick up Saturday,” so why is it asking? Asking about what you just said reads as deafness.

C · Shipped

Match the buyer's energy

Said it clearly: act. Maybe: a gentle offer. Didn't mean it: nothing. It plays back “here's how I read that” and searches.

You typeIt meansScoreThe agentIt asks
sectional couch near me, pick up Saturday, under $400Clearly local0.94Goes local-firstNothing. Acts and shows
sectional couchMaybe local0.68Normal results and a soft local cardA gentle chip
need a desk this weekCould go either way0.55Asks before searching“Pick up, or ship?”
real Rolex Submariner, check in personWants proof0.88Adds authenticationOne tip, then confirm
another barstool like last timeA repeat buyer0.74Reuses saved wishesLeaves an undo note
USB-C cable 2m braidedNot local at all0.08Stays out of the wayNothing

The rule that never bends: if it can't be undone (a trip, a payment, a meetup), the agent asks first. Every time, at any confidence.

Same spine on both threads. Act when sure, ask once when unsure, educate when the signal is weak, and never move money on its own. That spine is what AI Mode was built on.
05 · The move everyone missed

The data lives with the seller.

A clean buyer experience can't be bolted on at search time. Both fixes had to go upstream, to the listing. For size, that means verifying the product's actual size the moment a seller enters it. For local, it means showing sellers they can list for pickup, and why it pays.

Size
Fix it here

Seller listing

Capture a structured, verified size at the source, not free text.

→
So this works

Search & filter

Match on records we trust, not guesses.

→
And the buyer gets

Verified inventory

Search by size, see only what's confirmed to fit.

Local
Fix it here

Seller listing

Show sellers pickup is an option: a verified handoff and instant payout instead of $120+ freight.

→
So this works

Search & AI Mode

Hear “near me” and route to pickup inventory.

→
And the buyer gets

Pickup today

A code that releases payment only at the handoff.

✦
Educating the seller, at the moment it helps

3 buyers within 5 mi searched sectionals this week. Saturday morning is your strongest window. Suggested price: $360 to $395. Selling locally has to be less work than Facebook, or nobody lists and the shelf stays empty.

It read like fixation on small details. It was a cross-domain initiative with real return: verified seller data and new seller supply feeding a buyer experience that finally kept its promise.

07 · Why it compounds

One loop, both sides fed.

Buyer
searches, gets stuck, signals friction
Seller
clarifies the listing, lists better
eBay
  • Buyer friction on an attribute becomes a signal back to the seller: "you may want to clarify this."
  • Or the marketplace just fixes it. That's the job.
  • Buying informs selling. Selling informs buying. The loop keeps turning.
08 · The zoom out

Then search learned to understand intent.

Clean data unlocked the shift from a flat results page to an agent that asks first. Below, Auto runs the same three searches from the worked examples, and Nearby now runs a local pickup. Same spine: act when sure, ask once when unsure, and nothing is bought, bid, listed or sent without the shopper's OK.

✦

One box, twelve modes

Each mode attaches criteria to the item: a price to wait for, a pickup window, a look, a fit. When the shopper just types, Auto picks the mode.

✓

An agent that asks first

It asks two quick things when it has to, shows its steps, and stops before money moves. Nothing is bought, bid, listed or sent without the shopper's OK.

Comp · Nearby now pickup (Evo)

Some intent is local and fast: I need it tonight, or I'd like it sold this week. If an agent can coordinate a pickup against your calendar, the logical play is to turn local on. The rule that makes it safe: the agent shares its prediction before it acts, on both sides of the trade.

Buying agent · Nearby now
"I need a PS5 controller tonight. Is anyone selling one nearby?"
Sam can meet at 6:30pm, about 20 minutes from you. Want me to hold it and message Sam?
Hold & message SamNot yet
Selling agent · Nearby now
"I'd like to sell my desk chair this week. Can someone local pick it up?"
Here's my prediction: list it for local pickup and a buyer could be at your door in about 30 minutes. Want me to list it?
List itNot yet

Stated up front, following through reads as the feature, not the surprise.

11 · The ideas I set aside

The two I chose not to ship.

Each thread had a bolder version. Both were ambitious, and both simplified into what shipped.

Size and search

A game board of listings

Every listing a card, search a game board. Filters as piles, a deck you flip to tune your taste, a For-You hand that fans out. Built for wearables. Cards are a mental model every culture already shares.

Local intent

An immersive map

Local intent as a place, not a list: everything nearby on one map you explore first, with sellers, pickup windows and prices pinned where they are.

$389 · 0.9 mi $360 · 2.1 mi Today 5 to 8 PM
Simplified into: a short shelf with list and map, and “Why this” on every card.

Why they stayed concepts: both were heavy builds, not the lean, near-term play. Knowing which bold idea to set aside is part of the job. Both are still buildable, and the sponsored card wears its label in the open.
